projects.title: Book Genre Classification
projects.subtitle: Automating book genre prediction using NLP and Machine Learning
projects.description: This project focuses on automating the classification of books into appropriate genres using Natural Language Processing (NLP) and Machine Learning. The system takes a book's description as input and predicts its genre (e.g., Fiction, Mystery, Romance, Non-Fiction) by analyzing and learning from labeled training data. The dataset underwent rigorous preprocessing, including text cleaning, stopword removal, stemming, and TF-IDF vectorization to extract meaningful features. Multiple classification algorithms such as Logistic Regression, Naive Bayes, Random Forest, and Support Vector Machines (SVM) were trained and evaluated using metrics like accuracy, precision, recall, and confusion matrix to identify the best-performing model. The project also included comprehensive data preprocessing pipelines, feature engineering, visualization of model performance, and the development of an interactive script for testing custom book descriptions. I was primarily responsible for data preparation, visualization, system integration, and end-to-end pipeline implementation, while my teammate, Angel C J, led the model-building and training phase. Together, we successfully built a reliable and scalable genre classification system that achieved high accuracy and provided valuable insights into NLP-based classification tasks.
features: Comprehensive data preprocessing and feature engineering
Comparison of ML models using accuracy, precision, recall, and confusion matrix
Interactive script to test custom book descriptions

projects.title: MindMap

projects.title: Snake Game
projects.subtitle: Classic Snake Game built with HTML, CSS, JavaScript, and Pygame (Python).
projects.description: Developed two fully functional versions of the classic Snake Game to provide both online and offline gameplay experiences. The browser-based version, built using HTML, CSS, and JavaScript, is lightweight, responsive, and accessible through a live preview, allowing anyone to instantly play without installation. In parallel, I created a desktop version using Python’s Pygame library, which offers a richer offline arcade-style experience while retaining the same mechanics. Both versions feature smooth controls, dynamic difficulty scaling as the snake grows, real-time score tracking, and a modern user interface, giving players a nostalgic yet polished gaming experience while significantly enhancing my skills in JavaScript DOM manipulation, Python game development, and performance optimization techniques.

challenges.solution: Implemented collision detection with boundaries and self

results: Delivered a fully playable arcade-style game
Improved JavaScript DOM manipulation skills
Enhanced understanding of game loops and animations

projects.title: Neon Tic Tac Toe
projects.subtitle: A modern glowing Tic Tac Toe game built with HTML, CSS, and JavaScript
projects.description: An interactive and visually striking Tic Tac Toe game with a neon theme, designed to combine logic and aesthetics. The browser-based version is built using HTML, CSS, and JavaScript, where the core game logic is implemented in JavaScript while creative use of CSS animations and neon effects deliver a futuristic user experience. Additionally, a desktop version was developed using Python and Pygame, offering an offline mode with similar mechanics, interactive graphics, and responsive controls. Both versions emphasize problem-solving, modular coding practices, and creative front-end design.
